paragraphs.text: By the date of this prophecy, compared with Jer 27:12; Jer 28:1, it should seem that it lay dormant for fourteen or fifteen years ere it was recited.
paragraphs.anchor: In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Yokes with bonds, such as they are wont to be fastened with.
paragraphs.anchor: Make thee bonds and yokes

paragraphs.text: This was to the prophet, saith the Jesuit, molesta et probrosa poenitentia, {a} a troublesome and disgraceful penance. But this was no will worship, say we; and much handsomer than the penances they put the people to in Italy, where you may see them go along the streets, saith mine author, {b} with a great rope about their necks, as if they were dropped down from the gallows. And sometimes they wear a sausage or a swine’s pudding in place of a silver or gold chain, for a sign of their mortification, and that they may merit.
paragraphs.anchor: And put them upon thy neck.

paragraphs.text: {a} A Lapide.
{b} Bee Hive of Rome.

i.e., Ambassadors of those neighbouring states, who might come to Zedekiah, to confederate with him against Nebuchadnezzar’s growing greatness; but all in vain, and to their own ruin. Deus quem destruit dementat. The wicked oft run to meet their bane, as if they were even ambitious of destruction.
paragraphs.anchor: By the hand of the messengers

paragraphs.text: But they would not be warned, and were therefore ruined. So true is that of an ancient, Divinum consilium, dam devitatur, impletur: humana sapicuria, dum reluctatur, comprehendirut.
paragraphs.anchor: Go, tell your masters.

paragraphs.text: And I am therefore the great proprietary and Lord paramount of all, to transfer kingdoms at my pleasure. This Nebuchadnczzar, after seven years’ apprenticeship served among the beasts of the field, had learned to acknowledge. {Dan 4:23-25}
paragraphs.anchor: I have made the earth.

paragraphs.text: Nebuchadnezzar shall be monarch contra Gentes. Dicunt nugatores equitasse Nabuchodonosor super leonem, et infraenasse draconem. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: And now have I given all these lands.

paragraphs.text: {a} Oecolamp.
All the neighbouring nations, and some others more remote; but never was any man παντοκρατωρ, universal monarch, though some have styled themselves so, as did Sesostris King of Egypt:
paragraphs.anchor: And all nations shall serve him.

paragraphs.text: “ Qui Pharios currus regum cervicibus egit. ”
The greatest monarchies had their times and their turns, their rise and their ruin.
paragraphs.anchor: Until the very time of his land come.

paragraphs.text: As the Chaldeans had served themselves of the Assyrians, so did the Persians of the Chaldeans, the Greeks of the Persians, the Romans of the Greeks, the Goths and Vandals, and now the Turks, of the Romans; such an aestuaria vicissitudo there is in earthly kingdoms, such a strange uncertainty in all things here below. "Wherefore we receiving a kingdom which cannot be moved, let us have grace, whereby we may serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear." {Heb 12:28} Let us serve him, and not serve ourselves upon him, as self-seekers do.
paragraphs.anchor: And then many nations and great kings shall serve themselves of him.

paragraphs.text: It is better, then, to serve a foreign prince than to perish by the sword, famine, or pestilence. It should not be grievous to any man to sacrifice all his outward comforts to the service of his life.
paragraphs.anchor: And it shall come to pass that the nation, &c.

paragraphs.text: The Lord disposeth of the kingdoms of the heathens also, though in such a way as may seem to us to be mere hap hazard.
paragraphs.anchor: And that will not put their neck under the yoke.

paragraphs.text: By seeking to shun a less mischief, they shall fall into a greater; if they escape frost, they shall meet with snow.
paragraphs.anchor: That nation will I punish.

paragraphs.text: Whom the devil setteth to work to persuade you otherwise to your ruin; as he is an old manslayer, and hath his breathing devils abroad as his agents, such as are here mentioned.
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore hearken not ye to your prophets.

paragraphs.text: So it would prove; and such would be the event of their false prophecies.
paragraphs.anchor: To remove you far from your land.

paragraphs.text: When God bids us yoke, it is best to submit. In all his commands there is so much reason for them, that if God did not enjoin them, yet it were best, in self-respects, for us to practise them; since in serving him we shall have the creatures to serve us, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: But the nations that bring their neck.

paragraphs.text: See on Jer 27:1.
paragraphs.anchor: I spake also to Zedekiah.

paragraphs.text: Better do so than worse: if ye will not be active in it, ye shall be passive; and that because ye would not take upon you the lighter yoke of mine obedience.
paragraphs.anchor: Bring your necks under the yoke.

paragraphs.text: “ Deus crudelius urit
Quos videt invitos succubuisse sibi. ”
- Tibul. Eleg. 1.

Ec quae haec pertinacia? If thou hast no mercy on thyself, yet pity the State, which is like to perish by thy pertinace. Josephus highly commendeth Jeconiah for his yielding to go into captivity for the safety of the city. Tertullian giveth this counsel to Scapula the persecutor, If thou wilt not spare us, yet spare thyself; or, if not thyself, yet thy country, Carthage, which is like to smoke for thy cruelty, for "God is the avenger of all such."
paragraphs.anchor: Why will ye die, thou and thy people?

paragraphs.text: Quanta opus opera, saith Oecolampadius. What a business it is to beat men off from false prophets and seducers! But let the end and the evils they lead to be remembered. Cavete a Melampyge.
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore hearken not unto the words of the prophets.

paragraphs.text: When they speak a lie, they speak of their own, as it is said of their father the devil. {Joh 8:44 Jer 23:21-22}
paragraphs.anchor: For they prophesy a lie.

paragraphs.text: Behold, the vessels of the Lord’s house, &c.] Notorious impudence! but it hath ever been the lot of the Church to be pestered with such frontless dissolute fellows, who dare affirm things flat opposite to the truth, and flatter men in their sin to their utter ruin. Those who are of God can do nothing against the truth, but for the truth. {2Co 13:8}
Life and death is let in by the ear. {Isa 55:3} Take heed, therefore, what ye hear.
paragraphs.anchor: Hearken not unto them.

paragraphs.text: And so long as ye may have liberty of conscience upon any reasonable terms, be content; and not, as the bird in the cage, which, because pent up, beateth herself.
paragraphs.anchor: Serve the king of Babylon.

paragraphs.text: Let them pray in the Holy Ghost, by whom they pretend to be inspired. Let us see what answer. So Elias called upon the Baalites to call aloud unto their god; and forasmuch as he heard them not, the people were satisfied that they were false prophets. God will fulfil what he hath foretold; but then he looketh that his servants should make intercession. Elias had foretold Ahab that there should be store of rain after a long drought; but then he went up into Mount Carmel to pray for that rain. I came for thy prayer, said the angel to Daniel. God’s prophets are his favourites, and may have anything of him.
paragraphs.anchor: Let them make intercession to the Lord of hosts.

paragraphs.text: Till by my providence I appoint a great part of them to be brought back again, and to be new consecrated to my service. {Ezr 1:7; Ezr 7:19}
